decision_explanation: The small Unified Neural Policy's apparent outperformance over CARM Canonical (-23.97% -> +13.50%) is predominantly driven by passive cash exposure dampening (holding 90-95% cash) rather than learned asset selection alpha. When evaluated against exposure-matched baselines, simple rule-based controls (90% Cash + 10% BTC rebalanced weekly) achieve superior Sharpe (0.390 vs 0.324), higher Sortino (0.550 vs 0.453), significantly lower Max Drawdown (-9.23% vs -15.92%), and 10x lower transaction fees ($15 vs $143). Furthermore, the Shuffled-Signal falsification control achieved +16.04% net return, proving that the downside penalty in the cost-aware loss function drives the network into a permanent high-cash posture regardless of feature signal.
